processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Four ingots with nominal compositions Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr (x = 0, 2 wt%; y = 0, 3, 5 wt%) were prepared by vacuum induction melting under a high-purity Ar atmosphere. The 2Ni5Cr ingot has measured composition C 1.34, Si 0.37, Mn 20.8, P 0.010, S 0.002, Al 9.09, Mo 0.56, Ni 2.08, Cr 4.90, Ti 0.01, Nb 0.03, Fe Bal. (wt.%).
The as-cast ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h.
The ingots were hot-rolled to 4 mm-thick sheets with 95% thickness reduction. Initial rolling temperature 1040–1060 °C and finishing rolling temperature 950–970 °C.
The plate was online ultrafast cooled (UFCed) to ambient temperature with a cooling rate of ~40 °C/s, based on the efficient-use-water ultrafast-cooled device (ADCOS-PM) developed in-house.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized single-phase equiaxed FCC γ (austenite) structure containing a high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries; no B2 (BCC) phase detected. TEM dark-field images reveal nanosized long-range ordering (LRO) domains homogeneously distributed in the γ matrix (no κ-carbide satellite spots).

phases_present.grain_size: 7.60 μm (excluding twin boundaries); 2.2 μm (including twin boundaries)
phases_present.texture: no strong texture; high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries

grain_structure.texture: equiaxed grains with no strong texture (EBSD IPF)

precipitates.distribution: homogeneously distributed in the γ matrix

structures.overall_structure: Deformed/near-failure state: 2Ni5Cr steel exhibits LRO nanodomains; LRO domains are ellipsoidal with interconnected spinodal-type morphology.

precipitates.distribution: interconnected, homogeneously dispersed in γ matrix

interfaces.phase_evolution: Ni and Cr control the precipitation threshold of nanoscale κ-carbides and LRO domains. Adding Cr increases the formation energy of the carbides (e.g. Cr21(FeC3)2 formation energy −0.049 eV/atom, higher than (Fe,Mn)3AlC by 0.111 eV/atom), raising the nucleation energy barrier and suppressing carbide growth. Adding Ni lowers the formation energy (Ni-rich AlNi3C −0.181 eV/atom) and promotes κ-carbide formation. Consistent with this, the LRO domain/κ-carbide size decreases from ~10.69 nm (2Ni), ~5.46 nm (2Ni3Cr), ~2.14 nm (2Ni5Cr) to ~1.75 nm (3Cr).
interfaces.interface_notes: For 2Ni5Cr (highest Cr content) the ordered structure appears as fine LRO nanodomains rather than κ-carbides; superlattice intensities are weak, indicating a very low volume fraction (quantitative estimate not possible from DF because sheet thickness is uncertain).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: electrical discharge machined tensile specimens cut along rolling direction (RD); gauge length 25 mm, thickness 3 mm, width 7 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: crosshead speed 3 mm/min in a Gotech electronic universal testing machine with laser extensometer; at least three specimens per steel tested to fracture

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve shown in Fig. 4a (green 2Ni5Cr curve, terminates near engineering strain ~0.50); true stress–strain curve in Fig. 4b

strain_hardening_rate.value: three strain-hardening stages (I, II, III); Stage II prolonged compared with 2Ni/2Ni3Cr with increasing Cr content; 2Ni5Cr has higher Stage-III hardening rate than 2Ni and 2Ni3Cr

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: SEM fractography of the fibre zone

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: total elongation (increase with Cr addition relative to no-Cr 2Ni steel)
TS × TEL (GPa-%) = 59.94 GPa-% and YS = 1071 MPa for 2Ni5Cr sits in an otherwise empty upper-right region of the YS vs TS×TEL map, above the literature boundary

characterization_methods.technique: Electron back-scatter diffraction (EBSD) - IPF and phase maps
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Ultra55 scanning electron microscope; specimens vibration polished with 50 nm colloidal silica for 2.5–24 h (Buehler-VibroMet 2)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 20 µm scale bars on IPF/phase maps
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine grain structure, phase constitution and twin boundary fraction
characterization_methods.key_findings: 2Ni5Cr steel is fully recrystallized, single equiaxed FCC γ phase with a high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries and no B2 phase; average grain size 7.60 μm excluding twin boundaries (2.2 μm including twins).
2Ni5Cr trace shows only five FCC γ reflections — γ(111) (strongest), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311), γ(222) — with no B2/BCC reflection, confirming single-phase FCC γ austenite.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) - bright-field, dark-field and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai G2 F20 operating at 200 kV; TEM foils cut by EDM to 1 mm, ground to <80 μm, thinned by Struers TenuPol-3 double-jet in 10 vol% perchloric acid + 90 vol% ethanol at 20 V and −30 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal matrix phase and ordered structures (LRO domains/κ-carbides)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Bright-field images show γ austenite grains with straight twin boundaries; dark-field (from {110}LRO reflection) reveals very fine, low-contrast bright LRO domains; SAED shows very faint superlattice reflections at 1/2{0-22}γ and/or 1/2{200}γ with no satellite spots, indicating LRO domains rather than κ′-carbides.

characterization_methods.technique: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) with FFT and inverse-FFT (IFFT) reconstruction
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM along [011]γ zone axis; IFFT using {011} and {100} LRO superlattice reflections; domain sizes measured with Image-Pro Plus on >200 domains
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure size and morphology of LRO domains / κ-carbides
characterization_methods.key_findings: LRO domains in the 2Ni5Cr steel are ellipsoidal with an interconnected spinodal-type morphology; average LRO domain size ~2.14 nm (from ~10.69 nm for 2Ni, ~5.46 nm for 2Ni3Cr, ~2.14 nm for 2Ni5Cr, ~1.75 nm for 3Cr).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM; 200 µm scale bar on fibre-zone images
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 2Ni5Cr steel fibre zone shows a coarse, irregular dimpled microvoid-coalescence morphology with pronounced deep pits and prominent tear ridges, i.e. ductile fracture (no cleavage facets).

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical yield-strength model: linear summation of strengthening mechanisms with precipitate shearing (order, coherency, modulus-mismatch) contributions
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fully recrystallized Fe–Mn–Al–C steel; dislocation strengthening disregarded; d_eff taken from EBSD (2.2 μm for 2Ni5Cr); κ-carbide treated as a strong obstacle (A_s = 0.64)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated strengthening contributions compared with measured yield strengths (Fig. 11); predicted and measured yield strengths agree well, with solution strengthening the primary mechanism.

analytical_models.model_note: σ_0 = 3τ_0 with τ_0 = 2×10^-4 G; σ_ss = 279[C] − 1.5[Mn] + 20.5[Al] + 2.9[Ni] + 3.9[Cr]. Solution strengthening is the primary mechanism for all four samples.
σ_order contributes to σ_prep only in the 3Cr and 2Ni5Cr samples with LRO nanodomains, because some nanodomains are smaller than the critical size.

analytical_models.equation_role: σ_coh = Σ A_s M α_ε (G ε_c)^3/2 (r_i f_i / 0.5Gb)^1/2 (Eq. 3)
analytical_models.model_note: Part of the σ_coh + σ_mod pair that is dominant for the 2Ni5Cr steel.
For the 2Ni5Cr steel the dominant precipitation contribution is σ_coh + σ_mod; the peak σ_coh+σ_mod is ~19 MPa (dense cluster 1.0–2.4 nm) plus one isolated bar near 3.1 nm at ~21 MPa (Fig. 10d).
Red dashed transition line at ~1.0 nm separates σ_order from σ_coh+σ_mod domains for the 2Ni5Cr steel.

computational_details.simulation_method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) formation-energy calculations
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Possible κ-/carbide structures of the Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C steel family
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Formation-energy trends (Ni lowers, Cr raises) consistent with the DF TEM domain sizes in Fig. 1.

analytical_models.model_name: Formation energies of possible (κ-) carbide structures
analytical_models.equation_role: Ranking of phase stability by formation energy (eV/atom)
analytical_models.model_note: Cr addition raises κ-carbide formation energy (Cr21(FeC3)2 is 0.111 eV/atom higher than (Fe,Mn)3AlC), increasing the nucleation barrier; Ni reduces it (AlNi3C −0.181 eV/atom), promoting growth — explaining fine LRO domains in the high-Cr 2Ni5Cr steel.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 2Ni5Cr steel (wt.%): C 1.34, Si 0.37, Mn 20.8, P 0.010, S 0.002, Al 9.09, Mo 0.56, Ni 2.08, Cr 4.90, Ti 0.01, Nb 0.03, Fe Bal.
Combined strength–ductility figure of merit TS × TEL for the 2Ni5Cr steel is 59.94 GPa-% (Table 2).

The text of Section 3.2 states the total elongation 'increases from 34.1% to 54.5%' with Cr addition, which conflicts with the Table 2 value of 50.5% for 2Ni5Cr (and 54.4% for 3Cr); the tabulated 50.5% is treated as the 2Ni5Cr value.

The paper's abstract/plain statements of YS > 1100 MPa, UTS > 1200 MPa and TEL > 45% (e.g. conclusion item 1) are explicitly attributed to the 2Ni3Cr steel, not the 2Ni5Cr steel, and were therefore not assigned to this sample.

The detailed deformation-substructure TEM study (Figs. 6–8 and the Fig. 12 schematics) and the corresponding HDDA/DSBR conclusions were reported only for 3Cr and 2Ni steels; no equivalent strain-by-strain substructure analysis of the 2Ni5Cr steel is presented, so slip/deformation findings were not attributed to this sample.
